summary.text: 这 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 這, used for “this” and “here.” The traditional graph is also reported in an older verb use meaning “meet” or “receive,” but the evidence does not establish a link between that verb and the demonstrative.

formation.text: The demonstrative’s formation is unresolved. For traditional 這 in the separately reported verb sense “meet/receive,” one analysis treats 辶 as semantic and 言 as phonetic. A Warring States manuscript graph containing 酉、口、言 has also been proposed as 這 in that verb sense. These accounts do not establish how the demonstrative arose or how 这 was formed.

components.text: In the analysis of traditional 這 for the older verb “meet/receive,” 辶 is the semantic component, associated with going or movement. This does not establish its role in the demonstrative.
In that same analysis of traditional 這, 言 is proposed as the phonetic component. The available current readings provide a comparison but do not establish this ancient sound relation.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings are a modern comparison only; they do not independently establish 言’s identity as the historical phonetic component or its ancient sound relation to 這.

sound.text: Current Mandarin readings are zhè for traditional 這 and yán for 言. This pair records present-day readings, not proof of the proposed ancient phonetic relation.

history.text: The supplied evidence identifies 这 as the standardized simplified counterpart of 這, but does not give the date or graphic steps of standardization. No verified character-specific historical glyph image is available here.

A Warring States manuscript graph with 酉、口、言 has been interpreted as 這 used for the older verb “meet/receive.” This manuscript-specific reading remains a proposal. Accounts report that 這 is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and from Shuowen; a continuous graphic history is not established.

uncertainties.text: The source of the demonstrative remains unresolved. Proposals involve 者, 之, and 遮; reported Tang spellings and a proposed handwriting confusion with 遮 do not determine which account is correct.

The older verb and the demonstrative are documented separately. The evidence establishes neither a semantic bridge nor that the demonstrative borrowed its graph from the verb; the reported Tang examples have not been checked against their underlying dated texts.

Traditional 這 is analyzed with 言 as a phonetic component in the older verb use “meet/receive,” but no ancient reading pair establishes that proposed sound relation. The current Mandarin readings are yán for 言 and zhè for 這 and 这; they do not prove the historical analysis. Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ŋrans): semantic 辶 (“walk”) + phonetic 言 (OC *ŋan).
The character was originally a verb meaning “to meet”, whose modern pronunciation is yàn. It was later borrowed for the proximal demonstrative “this/here”, by a confusion in medieval handwriting with 遮 (zhē, “this”).
First attested in the Tang dynasty; etymology unclear. Proposed etymologies:
* From 者 (OC *tjaːʔ, “one which”) (Lü, 1985). Wang (1990) notes that 者 always occurs after what is referred to, whereas 這 always before.
*: 者 (OC *tjaːʔ, “one which”) > 者 (MC tsyaeX, “this (possessive case)”) > 者 (MC tsyaeX, “this (general demonstrative)”) > Mandarin 這 /这 (zhè).
* From 之 (OC *tjɯ, “this; it”) (Wang, 1990). Norman (1988) notes that this derivation would be phonologically problematic.

gaps: The cited dictionary reports 這 is absent from oracle-bone/bronze inscriptions and Shuowen, but this research did not inspect a dated manuscript image or establish the oldest attested graph for the older verb.

For the older verb reading ‘meet/receive’, 言 is described as phonetic in 這; no independently verified ancient pronunciation pair for 言 and 這 was established here. Do not substitute modern zhè for an ancient sound argument.

The demonstrative 這 is documented in Tang materials, but its source remains disputed: proposals involving 者, 之, and 以字形/書寫混淆與遮 were encountered, without adequate primary textual or phonological evidence to choose among them. The dossier’s specific claim of medieval handwriting confusion with 遮 was not independently verified.

No demonstrated semantic bridge links ‘meet/receive’ to proximal ‘this/here’; treat the verb and demonstrative histories separately. The demonstrative chronology is based on dictionary and secondary reports of Tang examples; exact manuscript dates were not independently checked.
The simplified form 这 is supplied as a simplified counterpart of traditional 這 in the dossier, but no character-specific official simplification-history source was successfully opened in this pass.

Official Unicode per-character Unihan pages for U+9019 and U+8FD9 were attempted but inaccessible. The exact supplied local kMandarin rows were checked; Unicode FAQ was inspected for field interpretation. Local repository files are not external citations.

The local Baxter–Sagart TSV search did not return either 這 or 这; no BS reconstructions for the character are asserted, and the file search result alone cannot establish that the dataset contains no relevant related-character rows.
No bulk-text reuse terms were verified for the repeatedly encountered websites; no local extract is recommended.
The older verb use and demonstrative use remain separate: the inspected dictionary does not establish a semantic bridge or demonstrate that the demonstrative borrowed the graph from the verb.
The Tang example is reported by the dictionary, but this pass did not inspect the dated manuscript or edition behind the citation.
The exact ancient object/word reading associated with proposed bronze/oracle-bone 言 graphs remains unsettled here; the surfaced scholarly article was not accessible for inspection.
No local primary readings rows or official per-character Unicode Unihan pages were verified in this browsing pass; modern readings and historical sound comparisons are therefore not asserted.

The Sinica query page did not render a specific 這 record, and searches did not establish a character-specific Commons file description page. No image candidate meets the required identity and provenance standard, so no glyph image is proposed.
The dictionary identifies 这 as the simplified counterpart of 這, but no inspected source in this pass establishes the dated standardization history.

limitations.text: No verified image shows a character-specific historical form of 這. The reported Warring States manuscript reading for the verb “meet/receive” remains a proposal, and the available glyph query provides no identifiable form. The older verb and the demonstrative “this/here” have no established graphic or semantic link in the available evidence.
